abi_formula.R_ARM_THM_MOVW_BREL: S+A-B(S), checked as an unsigned 16-bit complete value

rwpi_contract.checked_transformation: ordinary FOP shrinks checked_rwpi_worker from 28 to 26 bytes, retains 12 exact instruction origins and remaps the retained relocation offset by -2
rwpi_contract.default_policy: unsupported and whole-function retention because AAELF32 leaves B(S) platform-defined
rwpi_contract.explicit_policy: --firmbolt-arm-static-base=segment-start declares B(S) to be the referenced symbol's input PT_LOAD start
rwpi_contract.linker_gap: the pinned LLD classified R_ARM_THM_MOVW_BREL as static-base-relative but had no Thumb encoding or implicit-addend extraction case before this milestone
rwpi_contract.negative_control: the pinned linker rejects checked value 0x10000 with the exact legal range [0, 65535]; BOLT's relocation handler accepts 0xffff and rejects 0x10000
rwpi_contract.verification: reference and candidate both write RAM words [42, 42] under the Cortex-M3 FastDyn fixture

scope_limits: AAELF32 does not require B(S) to be a PT_LOAD start; this interpretation remains opt-in firmware metadata rather than an inferred universal rule
generic AArch32 JITLink source-object BREL remains unsupported until its graph API carries the static-base origin explicitly
R_ARM_THM_MOVW_BREL is a checked complete unsigned 16-bit static-base offset; it is not interchangeable with the truncating _NC half of a MOVW/MOVT pair
executable-target and otherwise movable BREL dependencies retain their original implementation
the production matrix demonstrates no regression across the existing firmware corpus, not complete x86-backend parity
the milestone establishes relocation, final-link publication and execution correctness, not a performance result

source.gnu_binutils_cross_check: GNU BFD rejects R_ARM_THM_MOVW_BREL when the computed value is at least 0x10000
source.note: B(S) is an implementation-defined addressing origin and need not be the segment base; the segment-start interpretation is therefore explicit
